title: The board won't bring Jensen Huang back, so I built a boardroom of 10 LLM directors you can argue with
author: No-Natural391
selftext:
You take one of the ten seats on Nvidia's board and argue to get Jensen reinstated. Six votes does it. The video is one real run, and I lost 5–5.

How it works:

* Each director is an LLM character with a starting stance (25% to 90% support), one thing they care about, and their own voice.
* The model doesn't only talk. Every turn it calls a function to move votes. If you interrupt someone, it also rules whether that was a "debate win" or a "protocol penalty". The game clamps the numbers so one line can't flip the room.
* Directors take turns arguing with Jensen on their own. You speak on your turn, or cut in, by typing or by holding the mic.
* Jensen is a separate character who answers whoever just spoke, and his mood changes his pose.

Nothing is scripted, but the board reliably scolds memes ("'line go up' is not a governance answer") and Jensen takes their side.

Built on Mopan, which I work on. Happy to explain any part.

comments.author: ZyronZA
comments.body:
I beg to differ! "Line go  up" and "Line go up and to the right" is all that matters in a bubble.

Cute game though.
